borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
decision_conditions: The proposed development would result in a significant reduction of the commercial floorspace of a unit within a primary frontage of the designated centre. The applicant has failed to demonstrate that the commercial unit, as a result of the loss of the ancillary utility and storage space, would still be able to continue to operate effectively, detracting from the viability and vitality of the unit and high street. The development is deemed to be unacceptable and contrary to:Paragraph 93 of the National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (DLUHC, December 2023)Policy E9 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policies DME3 and DME5 of the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan (September 2024)

The proposed development by reason of its scale, bulk, and mass, represents poor design, lacking articulation, visual interest and failing to respect the architectural design and character of the surrounding area,  thus would sit uncomfortably within the streetscene and at odds with the character of the area, contrary to: Paragraphs 131 and 135 of the National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (DLUHC, December 2023)Policies D1 and D4 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policies SP2, DMD1, DMD5 of the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan (September 2024)

The proposed development would create four inadequately sized, single aspect, studio apartments with no allocated built-in storage. This would present cramped units with poor access to passive ventilation. The sense of enclosure would be worsened due no provision of private external amenity space.  Further, the access into the flats would be poor requiring navigation down an unlit accessway, and also the building's entrance would open directly onto the access road, posing safety hazards to occupants, given the absence of a setback or pedestrian pathway. This arrangement fails to ensure safe and convenient access for future residents.  As such, this would create a substandard quality of accommodation, contray to:DCLG Technical Housing Standards (nationally described space standard) (DCLG, March 2015) (as amended)Policy D4, D6 and Table 3.1 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policy DMD1 of the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan (September 2024)Housing Design Standards LPG (June 2023)

The proposed development, by reason of its bulk, mass, scale and siting, would result in a detrimental loss of outlook, daylight and overshadowing to neighbouring properties, notably no.252a Oxlow Lane. As such, this is considered contrary to:Part D of policy D6 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policy DMD1 of the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan (September 2024)

The applicant has failed to demonstrate that the site would have capacity to provide secure and adequately located refuse and cycle storage for both the commercial unit and residential units individually resulting in littering which could negatively impact the amenity of the area and the users of the development. As such, this is considered contrary to:Policy T5 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policy DMT 2 and DMSI8 of the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan (September 2024)London Cycling Design Standards (September 2016)The Council's Planning Advice Note on Waste and Recycling Provisions in New and Refurbished Residential Developments (dated 20/05/2021)
description: Conversion of the rear of 250 Oxlow Lane into 4 studio flats involving the construction of a first floor rear extension, a new ground floor side entrance and the addition of fenestration on the side elevation
